text:
alex: Quick heads-up — kicking off the quarterly access review early next week. I ran a sweep and found a cross-account KMS grant for svc-legacy that dates to 2021 and ~14 user accounts with admin SSH keys that haven't rotated in >180d. Want to prune stale admin keys and remove unused KMS grants. Planning a dry-run first. :mag:

morgan: pls paste the queries you used so ops can reproduce.

alex: pasted below. ran from my laptop w/ read-only creds.
```bash
# list AWS KMS grants for prod keys containing svc-legacy
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/prod-main | jq '.Grants[] | select(.GranteePrincipal | contains("svc-legacy"))'

# quick check for old authorized_keys entries across homes (SSH RSA heuristic)
for u in /home/*; do grep -H "ssh-rsa" $u/.ssh/authorized_keys || true; done | xargs -r stat -c '%n %y' || true
```

jamie: two suggestions: (1) do a dry-run that produces a CSV of "candidate removals" with owner, last-seen, justification link; (2) auto-create a ticket for each candidate that requires owner approval within 7d before removal. if no owner, auto-revoke. :white_check_mark:

sasha: I can run the dev canary on Wed. I'll need the CSV and a small playbook to follow. ook to use svc-account svc-audit?

alex: yes please use svc-audit. I'll upload CSV to TICKET-7421 and mark sasha as canary owner. PR for the tooling changes (dry-run + csv export) is at https://git.redwood/pr/4789 — includes an auditor mode only.

infra-bot: scan-complete: id=scan-2026-03-18-01, candidates=18 (14 ssh keys, 4 kms-grants). report: https://internal/reports/scan-2026-03-18-01.json

morgan: quick question on KMS: some grants are cross-account for partner-data-ingest. We need to avoid breaking scheduled jobs. recommend we map grants to IAM roles and test access in a canary account first.

jamie: agreed. plan: test revoke in canary account, run partner ingest smoke tests, if OK proceed to prod revoke. Document rollback (recreate grant) and timestamp it.

sasha: playbook snippet — I'm pasting what I'll follow during canary: 
```
1) pull CSV from TICKET-7421
2) notify owners via the ticket template (auto-email) and set 7d justification window
3) for keys/grants with owners: run owner verification script (check last login, commit activity)
4) for ownerless: run revoke in canary, run smoke tests; if pass, schedule prod revoke during low-traffic window
5) log all actions to audit-log-prod and attach KMS revoke output to ticket
```

security-bot: policy-check: KMS logging retention is currently 90 days for some keys. Recommend bump to 365d for prod CMKs used across partners. Need security approval for retention cost. :warning:

alex: noted. I'll add retention bump to TICKET-7421 as a follow-up item and cc finance.

morgan: small nit — ensure we don't remove MFA-enabled human admin keys accidentally. filter for service accounts and non-mfa humans.

jamie: good call. add column "mfa_enabled" and require manual review for mfa=true.

sasha: canary window Wed 09:00-12:00 PT. volunteers for on-call in case rollback needed?

alex: I'll be on-call until 11:30. jamie can cover the rest.

morgan: I'll prepare monitoring dashboards (auth errors, failed jobs) and set alerts for spike >5% in the 30m post-revoke.

alex: next steps recap: (a) infra PR 4789 to land auditor CSV export (b) sasha runs dev canary Wed using svc-audit and playbook (c) jamie runs KMS revoke in canary then partner smoke tests (d) if canary green -> schedule prod revokes + retention change ticket. target finish: end of next week.

sasha: sounds good. I'll post a short log in ticket when canary starts. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket-update: TICKET-7421 assigned -> sasha, reviewers -> alex,morgan,jamie. due_date=2026-03-26

alex: thanks all — please keep messages short on the ticket and add evidence links. will run final sweep before any prod revoke.

morgan: ack.

jamie: ack.

security-bot: reminder: attach KMS CloudTrail snippets and grant IDs to the ticket for audit evidence.

alex: will do.
